Completed double-insurance declaration listing, per category, the other insurance company and policy number; the form marks this section as to be completed in every case
Payment instruction with payee name and address, IBAN and name of the financial institution
Insurer's written consent to an assignment of the benefit claim to a third party
Written substantiation of the claim for indemnity, where the insurer demands it (schriftliche Begruendung des Entschaedigungsanspruchs)

Insurer's prior consent to a repair whose expected cost exceeds the consent threshold
Insurer's instruction (Weisung / Anordnung) on the measures to be taken, and evidence that it was followed
Police consent to the removal or alteration of the Tatspuren
Insurer's consent to alteration of the damaged items before the loss is determined
Medical certificate (Arztzeugnis / aerztliche Bescheinigung) where a person was injured

Report to the insurer that stolen items have been recovered or news of them received
Insurer's declination of the claim for indemnity

non_evidentiary.reason: repair_r03 applies where a contractual claim restriction is at issue and requires determination of the Article 39 paragraph 2 number 2 exception before the restriction is treated as invalid. The challenged reservation preserves that same exception to the invalidity rule; repair_r03 operationalizes it under the narrower condition of a contractual shorter limitation or time restriction.

repair_r01 applies without any narrower condition and requires provision of the payment recipient's name and address, together with account details. Its fact and capability preserve the evidence-relevant consequence of recording and identifying the payment recipient; it imposes a stricter payment-recipient-information requirement than the challenged proposition alone.

repair_r01 requires provision of the payment recipient's account details, without any narrower condition. An IBAN is an account detail, so the existing rule preserves the same payment-administration evidence consequence under an equally broad applicability condition.

r03 expressly includes the condition that alterations to damaged property are contemplated before loss determination, supported by theft-source-0096#p1. It then requires preservation or proof that any alteration, disposal, or assistance use was authorized or justified. This is the same pre-assessment restriction and its evidence consequence.

r27 applies underinsurance analysis only where no applicable underinsurance waiver applies, and its condition is expressly supported by theft-source-0098#p1. CSS's waiver for household-contents damage therefore excludes the underinsurance comparison and proportional-indemnification evidence route preserved by r27.

The proposition is only an introductory cross-reference announcing that additional theft-or-robbery requirements follow. It states no particular duty, consequence, deadline, amount, proof route, or fact to establish. The operative follow-on requirements must be evaluated through their own propositions and rules.

r32 applies when a statutory or contractual duty is alleged to have been breached and requires establishment of the applicable duty, alleged conduct, culpability, agreed legal consequence, and impact on the loss. The stated duty of due care is such a duty; when its compliance can affect a legal disadvantage, r32 preserves the necessary duty-and-breach evidence analysis under the stricter condition of an asserted consequential breach.

r32 expressly includes the condition that a legal disadvantage for breach was agreed or otherwise applies, and theft-source-0108#p1 is listed as condition support. The rule then requires proof of the agreed legal consequence before any reduction or denial, preserving the proposition's exact evidence-relevant limitation.

Rule r44 applies when a claim arises from the insurance contract and requires assessment of the five-year period expressly subject to applicable statutory exceptions. Its supported_by field already includes theft-source-0131#p2. Thus r44 preserves the same reservation that paragraph 3 may qualify the five-year limitation rule under the same claim-from-insurance-contract condition.

Rule r03 governs contemplated alteration, removal, disposal, or other change to damaged property before loss determination and expressly preserves the exception where mitigation or public interests permit action. The challenged proposition is included in r03's supported_by and is reflected in r03's requirement, fact f05, and capability c06. The rule therefore preserves the identical exception under the same pre-determination damaged-property context.

Rule r03 has the condition that alteration at the loss location or to damaged property is contemplated before loss determination, and theft-source-0156#p1 is expressly one of its condition_supported_by propositions. The rule's preservation requirement, fact f05, and capability c06 preserve the evidence consequence of the challenged temporal scope under the same pre-determination condition.

repair_r06 applies where there are doubts about the beneficiary's entitlement to receive payment and requires determination of that entitlement before payment is directed. It therefore covers the same payment-recipient uncertainty stated here: uncertainty as to the person to whom the benefit may lawfully be paid necessarily presents doubt about that person's entitlement to receive payment.

r32 has the same operative condition: a statutory or contractual duty was breached and a legal disadvantage applies. Its supported condition expressly includes theft-source-0188#p1 and it requires determination of breach, culpability, impact, and the supported reduction or denial consequence. The challenged proposition's possible compensation reduction for violation of legal or contractual duties or provisions is thus preserved under the same or stricter applicability condition.
